comparator.academicYear: Prospective cohort sequence 2027–28 to 2029–30, checked 2026-09-25; 2026–27 OER used solely to resolve minor-credit ambiguity, not to guarantee prospective year-three course offerings
comparator.route: Ordinary non-abroad Linguistics bachelor with first-listed supplementary linguistics minor packages in year two
comparator.sourceNotes: The prospective year pages total 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of twelve required 5-EC linguistics and supporting methods/AI courses; zero-credit academic language and mentoring entries are excluded. Year two consists of six required 5-EC linguistics courses (30 EC) and two required 15-EC arts minors. The selected supplementary linguistics minor 1 uses the first three listed 5-EC courses (language developmental disorders, language and thought, social interaction); minor 2 lists exactly three 5-EC courses (speech/voice/hearing, Dutch as a second language and Python). The prospective page mistakenly labels each individual supplementary-minor heading 30 EC, whereas its prose requires two minors of 15 EC each and the adopted 2026–27 OER independently states a 30-EC total year-two minor. Treating the headings as additive would give 90 EC for year two, contradicting both sources and the programme total. The ordinary, non-abroad prospective year three includes 5 EC language proficiency, 10 EC professional development, 5 EC language norms, a 10-EC research thesis and 30 EC genuinely free space; the abroad variant is not combined. The 2026–27 OER names different year-three taught major units (Pragmatics and History of Dutch) from the indicative 2029–30 webpage (Language proficiency and Language norms). This is a difference between distinct academic years, not evidence that 2029–30 has a guaranteed adopted curriculum. The selected route follows the prospective year pages, and the formal OER is cited only for the second-year 30-EC minor-space total.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary non-abroad Linguistics bachelor with first-listed supplementary linguistics minor packages in year two
routeSelection.basis: The generic Linguistics bachelor has two prospective third-year routes; select the first listed ordinary non-abroad route. For the second-year 30 EC restricted minor choice, select the numbered supplementary linguistics minors and their first three 5-EC options in official order. This selects disciplinary depth without reference to UCR fit, while the 30-EC third-year free space remains open.

exception.reason: The bachelor requires 60 EC of first-year foundations in the structure, acquisition, processing and disorders of human language; another 30 EC of core corpus, phonetic, sociolinguistic, experimental, semantic and syntactic analysis in year two; and a 10-EC independent linguistics thesis. The selected two arts minors deepen speech/language disorders, language and thought, second-language teaching and linguistic methods for 30 EC. Even allowing a genuinely open 30 EC third year, UCR has no coherent foundational sequence in phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantic theory, corpus linguistics, sociolinguistics or language pathology. A 24-course response built mostly from communication, psychology, AI and data science would replace the subject with neighbouring fields.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2027–30 prospective year-page route adds to exactly 180 EC, with 60 required in year one; 30 core plus two 15-EC restricted minor packages in year two; and 30 taught/research requirements plus 30 truly free EC in the non-abroad third year. The official year-two webpage’s individual “30 EC” minor headings are a layout/data error: the same page says each minor is 15 EC and the 2026–27 OER confirms 30 EC total minor space. The 2026–27 OER has different third-year course names from the prospective 2029–30 webpage, so no claim is made that its exact third-year units govern the later cohort.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 enriched UCR course rows, with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies acquisition, processing and neurocognitive language factors; MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning considers linguistic choices in texts; MCCCOMM111/213/311 study rhetoric and persuasion; MCCCOMM112 teaches basic Dutch; HCBCOGN311 includes language among other higher cognitive functions. DISGATE101 covers Python, DISDATA311 discusses language models within neural networks, BENGATE102 and HCBPSYC211 offer research/statistics, and GOSSOCI212 provides qualitative methods. These are discrete neighbouring perspectives. The workbook has no stand-alone phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, corpus linguistics, sociolinguistics, language-disorder or experimental linguistics progression. It therefore cannot underpin a credible 24-course Linguistics alternative despite useful cognitive, communication and computational components.
